inputs.question: In low- and middle-income countries, do programmes meant to improve education for children and young people with disabilities work, and which kinds work best?
inputs.scope:
Covers: Evaluated programmes and interventions in low- and middle-income countries aimed at improving educational access, participation or learning for children and young people (roughly school age through youth) with disabilities. It compares which intervention types have evidence of effect and how strong that evidence is.
Out of scope:
- Whether inclusive education is a human right or required under the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (Article 24) (That is a legal and normative question, not an empirical question about whether programmes work.)
- Effectiveness of disability-education programmes in high-income countries (The question is restricted to low- and middle-income settings, where contexts, resources and evidence bases differ.)
- Clinical or medical treatment of specific impairments (e.g. surgery, therapy for autism) without an education outcome (The page concerns educational outcomes, not health or rehabilitation outcomes in themselves.)
- Prevalence of disability among children in LMICs and the size of the out-of-school gap (This is descriptive background, not a test of whether interventions work.)
- Cost-effectiveness rankings across all education interventions for all children (This page judges programmes for disabled learners, not general education investment priorities.)
